subject: Re: MSA redlines — egregious conduct carve-outs and evidence gating
messages:
From: Rachel Stuart <rachel.stuart@acmecorp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Ellsworth <david.ellsworth@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MSA redlines — fraud/willful misconduct carve-outs

Vanessa,

Attaching our consolidated redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx). We have two open items where we need Redwood's position before we proceed:

1) Egregious conduct carve-out: ACME's position is that fraud, willful misconduct and intentional data exfiltration should be carved out from contractual liability caps and consequential damages exclusions. We expect unfettered recovery where such conduct is proven.

2) Evidence standard / gating: given the seriousness of uncapped exposure, ACME wants a defined evidence path — specifically a forensic investigation and a standard of "clear and convincing evidence" before invoking the carve-out.

Quick asks: can Redwood accept uncapped liability for proven fraud/willful misconduct, and will Redwood agree to an evidence protocol (third-party forensic review + written findings) rather than a bare claims-based standard?

We need to resolve these items this week to keep the procurement timeline intact.

Thanks,
Rachel Stuart
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Retail

Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (word redline)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Stuart <rachel.stuart@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — fraud/willful misconduct carve-outs

Rachel — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Rishi and Laura to get legal sign-off and commercial trade-offs on our side.

High level from Redwood: we are prepared to accept an uncapped exposure for proven fraud and for proven willful misconduct that is narrowly defined and evidenced. We need operational guardrails to avoid opportunistic claims:

- Evidence gating: propose a two-step process — (1) written notice + 30-day internal remediation/investigation window; (2) if unresolved, mutually-agreed third-party forensic review (selected from a short list) whose report will determine whether the carve-out applies.
- Standard: we prefer "preponderance of the evidence" for initial determinations and the independent forensic report as the dispositive step (rather than an absolute "clear and convincing" legal standard).
- Materiality threshold for gross negligence claims: propose a de minimis waiver and an aggregate threshold (e.g., claims below $100k except for data security events).

If ACME can accept the two-step gating that ends with a third-party forensic determination, we can move forward with uncapped carve-out language for fraud/willful misconduct. Laura — please flag any compliance or audit log requirements.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME MSA redlines — fraud/willful misconduct carve-outs

Short and commercial: this is a priority deal — Acme is our Q2 strategic account. I support Vanessa's compromise: uncapped for proven fraud/willful misconduct, but we accept an aggregate commercial cap for gross negligence (12 months fees) and require the forensic gating.

If Laura signs off on the operational gating language I authorize us to send the proposed clause to ACME. We should keep negotiations tight and avoid opening other liability bucket discussions.

Rishi
VP, North America Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Stuart <rachel.stuart@acmecorp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Ellsworth <david.ellsworth@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — follow up on gating and materiality

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple items from ACME's side:

- Mediation/multi-step delay: ACME is concerned that a long internal investigation window + mediation could delay remedies in live incidents (e.g., confirmed data exfiltration). We are willing to accept a short investigation window but want a hard stop (30 days) before Redwood can assert remediation as a defense to damages.
- Materiality threshold: for gross negligence we propose a carve-in when the incident either (a) leads to regulated data exposure (PI, payment data), or (b) causes direct financial loss > $250,000.
- Evidence standard: ACME prefers "clear and convincing" (not preponderance). Attached is a short memo explaining why the higher standard is important where caps are being carved out (evidence_standard_memo.pdf).

If Redwood can accept the 30-day hard stop + clear and convincing standard for the carve-out trigger, ACME will agree to the proposed aggregate cap for gross negligence (12 months fees) and to a limited consequential-damages carve-out only for the egregious conduct categories.

Rachel
Attachment: evidence_standard_memo.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Stuart <rachel.stuart@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed compromise language and next steps

Team — based on the back-and-forth, below is Redwood's proposed compromise language to drop into the MSA. If ACME agrees we will incorporate into the next redline and route to DocuSign.

--- proposed clause (for insertion) ---
1) Carve-out for Egregious Conduct: Notwithstanding any caps or limitations set forth herein, neither Party shall be limited in liability for proven fraud, willful misconduct or intentional data exfiltration.
2) Evidence Gate: A carve-out under (1) requires: (a) written notice; (b) a 30-day investigative period during which the Parties will cooperate in good faith; and (c) if the Parties cannot resolve the matter within 30 days, an independent third-party forensic investigation (selected from a mutually agreeable list) whose written findings shall be binding as to whether the carve-out applies.
3) Standard of Proof: The Parties agree that the independent forensic report is dispositive. For purposes of initial determinations a preponderance standard applies; however, where a court or arbitrator is asked to adjudicate the matter, the Parties reserve their respective legal standards.
4) Gross Negligence: Claims characterized as gross negligence shall be subject to an aggregate cap equal to twelve (12) months of average fees paid by Customer under the Order Form, except where such claim qualifies under (1).
5) Materiality: For purposes of this MSA, a "material" security incident includes: (i) unauthorized access to regulated personal data or payment information, or (ii) direct quantifiable losses exceeding $250,000.
6) No waiver of injunctive relief: Nothing herein prevents either Party from seeking injunctive relief in the event of imminent or ongoing data exfiltration.
--- end proposed clause ---

Questions for legal: Laura — are you comfortable with the forensic report being binding? Do we need to tweak the Standard of Proof line to give Redwood more protection in court? If ACME insists on "clear and convincing" in the MSA text we may need to tighten the forensic-selection mechanics.

If Laura is OK, I'll send this over to Rachel with a request for confirmation on the 30-day hard stop language.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed compromise language and next steps

Vanessa — language looks good, belt-and-suspenders approach makes sense. A few minor edits I would make before sending to ACME:

- Make the third-party selection process explicit: each Party proposes two vendors, mutually select one within 7 days, otherwise a neutral (e.g., JAMS list) appoints.
- Clarify that the forensic report is binding for purposes of applying the contractual carve-out but does not preclude either Party from seeking judicial review.
- Replace the phrase "preponderance" with "substantial evidence" for the internal determination to better reflect forensic practice (we can defend that in negotiations).

If agreeable, I authorize Vanessa to send with these tweaks and request confirmation on the 30-day hard stop. Once ACME agrees, we can prepare the DocuSign packet.

Laura Bennett
Contracts Counsel
Redwood Inference
